title: Prospect Intercept Signal Playbook: Rapid Field Probes for Emergent Model Features
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Market signals indicate a rapid emergence of niche LLM features (fine-grained tool calling patterns, ultra-short-context optimizations, and specialized instruction-following modes) among small model providers. We lack a lightweight, repeatable runbook to detect whether these features materially change buyer preferences or generate procurement triggers for Dedicated/Private offerings.

Hypothesis: Short, targeted field probes (3-week sprints) that combine prospect interviews, synthetic workload tests, and lightweight telemetry will identify high-confidence emergent features and the buyer pain they relieve. This will allow Product to prioritize integration efforts or signal go/no-go procurement of model variants.

Goals:
- Create a reproducible 3-week playbook for prospect intercepts and telemetry probes.
- Produce a prioritized list of 6 emergent features with buyer impact annotations and recommended product responses (monitor, integrate, or deprioritize).
- Deliver a readiness brief for sales/success with recommended talking points and a shortlist of 2 competitive mitigation experiments.

Success metrics:
- 12 prospect interviews completed across SMB and mid-market within the sprint.
- 2 synthetic workload benchmarks run for each candidate feature with latency/cost delta captured.
- Clear buyer impact tag for >=4 features (high/medium/low).

Scope & approach:
1) Intake and signal synthesis (3 days): harvest signals from telemetry (console search terms, eval regressions), support tickets, AE notes, and public release notes. Produce a 1-page candidate feature slate.
2) Design probe artifacts (4 days): short survey + 45-minute interview guide, one synthetic workload per feature, telemetry dashboard template (latency, cost, error surface).
3) Field probes (9 days): run interviews (target 12), run synthetic tests on 2 representative models per feature (one open, one vendor), gather screenshots and sample outputs.
4) Synthesis and recommendations (3 days): prioritize features, map to product levers (runtime, routing, quantization, API), and propose 2 rapid experiments for sales/solutions.

Data sources: Redwood Console logs, customer conversations (CRM), public changelogs, GitHub release notes for open models, synthetic workload harness (bench-runner), early-access partners.

Deliverables:
- 1-page Candidate Feature Slate (artifact link placeholder).
- Probe artifacts (survey + interview guide + synthetic workload configs).
- Final synthesis doc with prioritization table, recommended experiments, and exec summary.
- Sales brief and 2 short demo scripts for Solutions.

Stakeholders: Product (PM lead), Research (2 UX interviews), Applied ML (synthetic workload design), Eng (bench support), GTM (2 SDR/AEs for prospect intros).

Out of scope: Deep R&D to build model-level features; this is strictly discovery and rapid validation for prioritization.

Risks: Recruitment friction for prospect interviews; signal noise from internal feature requests; synthetic workloads may not generalize across all deployments. Mitigations include AE warm intros, prioritizing repeatable telemetry queries, and running tests across two hardware targets.

Next steps:
- Approve estimate and allocate research/bench cycles (PM -> ENG/APPLIED ML).
- Schedule AE outreach and initial prospect roster by 2026-03-01.
